title: Derived stalk of an oriented direct image is Milnor-tube cohomology
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Use small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and their left oriented product $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Put $Z=X\times_SY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\psi_{f,g}:Z_{\mathrm{Et}}\to P$ be the geometric morphism specified by the two projections and their equality over $S$; on a site triple $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ its inverse image is the sheaf represented by $U\times_VW$. Let $x,y$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point] of $X,Y$, and choose a specialization $c:g(y)\to f(x)$, meaning a morphism $S_{(g(y))}\to S_{(f(x))}$ of $S$-schemes between their strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], equivalently the corresponding $2$-morphism of geometric points in the convention of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Let $z:\mathbf{Set}\to P$ be the resulting point. The composite $Y_{(y)}\to S_{(g(y))}\xrightarrow{c}S_{(f(x))}$ defines $M=X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(f(x))}}Y_{(y)}$, with its natural map $r:M\to Z$. For every bounded-below complex $K\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of constant $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a canonical isomorphism in $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$
$$z^*R\psi_{f,g,*}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(M_{\mathrm{Et}},r^*K).$$
Here $R\psi_*$ and $R\Gamma$ are total right derived functors, computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $r^*$ is exact derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. The displayed isomorphism is induced by restriction from the affine pointed triple neighbourhoods of $z$ to their inverse limit $M$, and is natural in $K$.

source.place: Illusie, Around the Thom--Sebastiani theorem, section 1.3, formula (1.3.1) and the preceding paragraph, printed p. 7 (PDF page 7); morphism psi and inverse-image formula in section 1.2, (1.2.1), printed p. 5. Read from work/illusie-nearby-cycles28.pdf. Local corroboration in literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Expose XI: 1.4 (points of the oriented product), proof of Proposition 2.3 (fibre at a point as colimit over neighbourhoods (U -> V <- W)), and 4.3 (Psi^{-1}(U -> V <- W) = U x_V W).

proof.text: The universal property [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal] constructs $z$ from $(x,y,c)$, and constructs $\psi$ from the projections of $Z$ with their equality over $S$. Its inverse-image formula gives $\psi^{-1}(h_T^\#)=h_{U\times_VW}$ for a triple $T=(U\to V\leftarrow W)$. Apply [lem-trf-oriented-affine-neighbourhood-limit] to choose a small skeleton $I$ of the initial cofiltered category of affine pointed triples. Write $D_i=U_i\times_{V_i}W_i$, $t_i:D_i\to Z$ and $q_i:M\to D_i$. That node gives precisely $M=\lim_I D_i$, the maps $t_iq_i=r$, affineness of all $D_i$, affine transition maps, and etaleness of $t_i$. We will use the inverse category $I^{\mathrm{op}}$ for all section colimits.

source.place: Illusie, Around the Thom--Sebastiani theorem, §1.3, paragraph immediately preceding (1.3.1), printed p. 7; §1.2, inverse image of a triple after (1.2.1), printed p. 5. Read the author PDF in the browser; the copy named by earlier source metadata is absent locally. Oriented site/point conventions corroborated by literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé XI, 1.1, 1.6, 1.8.

proof.text:
The category of constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves on $Z_{\mathrm{Et}}$ has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]. Choose a bounded-below complex $J$ of injectives with $QJ\cong K$, using [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. It computes $R\psi_*K$ as $\psi_*J$ by [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Apply the general point formula [lem-trf-site-point-fibre], with $p=z$ and its initial affine neighbourhood category. In each degree adjunction and the inverse-image formula of Step 1 identify $(\psi_*J^m)(T_i)$ with $J^m(D_i)$. Therefore the complex
$$L=\varinjlim_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}J(D_i)$$
represents $z^*R\psi_*K$. The differentials are restrictions of those of $J$, so these identifications are identifications of complexes, not only of their groups.

source.place: Tag 0GIT, lemma-colimit-complexes; application to the oriented point described in Illusie §1.3, (1.3.1)

proof.text:
Exactness of the colimit functor from [lem-trf-site-point-fibre] identifies the kernels of $d^n$ and the cokernels defining their quotients by images with the colimits of the corresponding kernels and cokernels. Consequently
$$H^n(L)=\varinjlim_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}H^n(J(D_i))$$
for every integer $n$. This is the usual kernel/image computation of cohomology for an exact additive functor.

source.place: Tag 0GIT, lemma-colimit-complexes; application to the oriented point described in Illusie §1.3, (1.3.1)

proof.text:
For each etale object $D_i\to Z$, [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] identifies the underlying abelian group of $H^n(J(D_i))$ with $H^n(R\Gamma_{D_i}(VK))$, where $V$ forgets scalars. To identify object-cohomology with cohomology on $D_i$, take a bounded-below abelian injective representative $B$ of $VK$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-over-object-localization], restriction of each $B^m$ to $Z_{\mathrm{Et}}/D_i$ is injective; hence the restricted bounded-below complex computes its derived sections. The site equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies that slice with $(D_i)_{\mathrm{Et}}$, and under it the slice restriction of each $B^m$ is $t_i^{-1}B^m$ by the natural isomorphism $\rho$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction], which is exact, so $t_i^{-1}B$ represents $t_i^*VK$. Termwise sections in both descriptions are $B(D_i)$. Finally [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] identifies $t_i^*VK$ with $V(t_i^*K)$, and [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] on $D_i$ gives
$$H^n(J(D_i))\cong H^n(D_{i,\mathrm{Et}},t_i^*K).$$
These are the canonical restriction comparisons: localized restriction sends a section to that same section, and the two scalar-forgetting comparisons commute with object restrictions and with global cohomology pullback. Thus they commute both with transition maps and with pullback along $q_i$. No claim that forgetting scalars preserves injectivity is used.

source.place: Tag 0GIT, lemma-colimit-complexes; application to the oriented point described in Illusie §1.3, (1.3.1)

proof.text:
Construct the comparison itself before testing its cohomology. Exact inverse image $r^*$ of [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] sends $J$ to a representative of $r^*K$. Choose a K-injective resolution $r^*J\to A$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Identifying $J(D_i)$ with $\Gamma(D_i,t_i^*J)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] (clause 2: the unit is restriction), restriction along $q_i$ gives compatible chain maps $J(D_i)\to\Gamma(M,r^*J)\to\Gamma(M,A)$. Their colimit gives
$$\alpha:L\longrightarrow\Gamma(M,A),$$
whose target represents $R\Gamma(M,r^*K)$. Under Step 4, the map induced by $\alpha$ on $H^n$ is the colimit of the canonical derived pullback maps $H^n(D_i,t_i^*K)\to H^n(M,r^*K)$: these are defined by the inverse-image unit followed by the derived sections comparison, precisely the restriction and resolution maps just used. The pullback compatibility in [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] verifies this assertion after forgetting scalars, which is faithful on module homomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0GIT, lemma-colimit-complexes; application to the oriented point described in Illusie §1.3, (1.3.1)

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-etale-cohomology-limit] with base $Z$, system $(D_i)_{i\in I}$ and the bounded-below abelian complex $VK$. Its small cofiltered index, qcqs stages, affine transitions and limit $M$ are exactly those supplied in Step 1; no qcqs assumption on $Z$ is needed. It makes
$$\varinjlim_{I^{\mathrm{op}}}H^n(D_i,t_i^*VK)\longrightarrow H^n(M,r^*VK)$$
an isomorphism for every integer $n$. The inverse-image comparison [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] and the bounded-below sections comparison [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] identify this map with the underlying abelian map of $H^n(\alpha)$ in Step 5. Forgetting scalars preserves these filtered colimits: an element is a class of an element at one stage, and the scalar action is applied at that same stage. A bijective $\Lambda$-linear map has $\Lambda$-linear inverse. Hence $H^n(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism of $\Lambda$-modules for every $n$.

source.place: Tag 0GIT, lemma-colimit-complexes; application to the oriented point described in Illusie §1.3, (1.3.1)

proof.text: The map $\alpha$ is thus a quasi-isomorphism, so becomes an isomorphism in the localization defining $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Under Step 2 it has the required source and under Step 5 the required target. It is the comparison induced by restrictions to the limit, since each coprojection $J(D_i)\to L$ followed by $\alpha$ is exactly that restriction followed by the resolution map. The functorial K-injective resolutions of [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] make this construction natural on complexes. For a different injective representative of $K$, comparison through a common resolution gives the same derived morphism: the natural transformation from termwise sections to derived sections, and its uniqueness, are those of [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective]. Both source and target invert quasi-isomorphisms, so the natural comparison descends to $K$ in the derived category and is independent of choices.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact constant-coefficient inverse image, including underlying abelian and adjunction-unit comparisons.
Generic bounded-below evaluation/scalar-forgetting with pullback compatibility; prevents changing coefficient categories silently.
Generic injective preservation under site localization, used to evaluate complexes on an etale object.
Bounded-below continuity over the affine Milnor-tube presentation; the trace unit does not reprove general etale inverse-limit continuity.
Equivalence of the localized small etale site with the small etale site of an arbitrary etale object, not just an open immersion.

Generic functorial K-injective resolution existence on small ringed sites.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q35-c0842a826 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement, ILO XI 1.6/1.8/2.3/4.3 (pdftotext), Stacks 00YA and 0GIT, and the Mathlib Point/Basic.lean source. The item statement is unchanged from base, so no target is weakened. The specialization convention (c: S_(g(y))->S_(f(x)) as the 2-arrow gy=>fx) and psi^{-1}(T)=U x_V W agree with ILO. Coefficients stay as constant Lambda-modules: every passage to abelian groups goes through the bounded-below evaluation/forget and constant inverse-image nodes. Both new nodes are true, are not duplicates and do not restate a clause of the item. The affine-neighbourhood lemma checks out: initiality via affine V' containing c^*v; etaleness via the open diagonal of V/S; the limit through c; tested on the point case, on a trait with Z empty, and on f=id with nontrivial c giving an empty M and a zero stalk. The site-point lemma follows from Stacks 00YA(2) plus filtered colimits of modules; its Mathlib candidate is correctly not a leaf. Steps 1-7 check, including the continuity hypotheses (Z arbitrary, affine stages, cofiltered index). One fix: steps 4 and 5 used, without citing it, that slice restriction to D_i is t_i^{-1} and that the unit is restriction. I added lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction to both steps' uses, to proof_deps and to split_report.tool_uses. I accept the 7 declared generic tool uses plus this one. No SGA source is used.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
